content.comment_body: Hello, sorry for my basic question, but could someone clarify what exactly an open connector is and in which situations I should use it? Thanks in advance.

Did you check the help section for the block? Everything is explained there. Some blocks require the output to be connected even if you don't actually use the output. That's when open connectors are needed. If the output isn't connected, you won't be able to upload the software to the device. For example, with the message block, leaving the output unconnected causes an error when uploading. Connecting the output to an open connector resolves the issue and lets everything work.

Hi [user_name], thanks for your feedback. Let me explain the reason open connectors are required! [product_name] function blocks operate on a platform similar to Java, where each block has multiple inputs and always exactly one output, even if it’s just a message text. Successful execution of a function block requires that all inputs and outputs are defined or terminated. The open connector is used to terminate an output that doesn't need to be connected elsewhere. Outputs, digital markers, and analog flags can also serve as terminators but are best not used, as it wastes valuable programming resources. In simulation mode on a PC, terminations are less critical because the thread environment handles everything. However, on the microcontroller inside the [product_name], missing terminations will prevent download or compilation because the thread environment expects definitions for all outputs. If you run out of open connectors, you can use OR gates in a cascade to have one open connector serve multiple terminations. For analog signals, you can use an analog threshold trigger as a placeholder, with its output tied to an open connector. While it may seem inefficient, this method works. I heard at a recent trade fair that the next [product_name] will offer more open connectors, making things simpler. Happy programming!

analysis.insight_summary: Participants highlight that open connectors are essential for properly terminating unused outputs in block-based programming for [product_name] devices. Without connecting these outputs, uploading or compiling to the microcontroller will fail, due to strict requirements in the device's runtime environment. Simulations on a PC do not have this restriction, offering more flexibility.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking to understand why and when open connectors are necessary and expects clearer guidance on their use. They also hope future software versions or interfaces will make handling these termination requirements easier.
